+## Git State
+
+The `git_state` module will show in directories which are part of a git
+repository, and where there is an operation in progress, such as: _REBASING_,
+_BISECTING_, etc. If there is progress information (e.g., REBASING 3/10),
+that information will be shown too.
+
+### Options
+
+| Variable           | Default            | Description                                                                                                      |
+| ------------------ | ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
+| `rebase`           | `"REBASING"`       | The text displayed when a `rebase` is in progress.                                                               |
+| `merge`            | `"MERGING"`        | The text displayed when a `merge` is in progress.                                                                |
+| `revert`           | `"REVERTING"`      | The text displayed when a `revert` is in progress.                                                               |
+| `cherry_pick`      | `"CHERRY-PICKING"` | The text displayed when a `cherry-pick` is in progress.                                                          |
+| `bisect`           | `"BISECTING"`      | The text displayed when a `bisect` is in progress.                                                               |
+| `am`               | `"AM"`             | The text displayed when an `apply-mailbox` (`git am`) is in progress.                                            |
+| `am_or_rebase`     | `"AM/REBASE"`      | The text displayed when an ambiguous `apply-mailbox` or `rebase` is in progress.                                 |
+| `progress_divider` | `"/"`              | The symbol or text which will separate the current and total progress amounts. (e.g., `" of "`, for `"3 of 10"`) |
+

body: Are the prefix and suffix set this way specifically because they're meant to be used right next to the other `git` modules? I think we usually go for something like " on " or " in " for defaults.
I love seeing explanations for when panics occur or why things are safe. :+1:

IIRC, if there's a TOML option by the name, then the value is overridden with that value. Does that mean we've created (unintended, undocumented) TOML options here which could break the module if they were set?
Well. That is one monster of a function, and you've written it beautifully. 10/10, would read again.
It's not a big deal if the answer is "yes," it's just going to be a mental note in the 1.0 refactor to have ways to avoid this.

Ah, good point. I actually missed that `new_module` checked the `disabled` setting. 👍 

I'll fix that shortly.

body: I guess all modules implicitly do. I will update the docs 😄

Honestly, this choice was mostly to ensure that the prompt doesn't get too long. In the default prompt order, this comes directly after the branch name, so it usually makes sense it context.

That said, I'm happy to make changes if people think there are better options..?
Yeah, the answer is yes. I think this issue affects most modules in some form or another.

I think this is a fine compromise to make for now. I think at some point in the future, we're going to have to start adding shell adapter code that tells starship what size the terminal is, and let starship decide what gets sacrificed if the terminal is too small to fit everything.

(I also seem to recall properly handling SIGWINCH being a PITA, so I'm really looking forward to that...)
Alright, we'll kick that particular can down the road for now then.
